name: Vinegar
overview: Scripture presents vinegar as a substance with varied significance, both practical and symbolic. It was used in daily life, as seen when Boaz invited Ruth to dip her bread in vinegar during a meal, highlighting its role in food (Ruth 2:14). Vinegar was also explicitly forbidden to Nazarites as part of their vow of separation (Numbers 6:3), underscoring its distinct place in holiness practices. Most poignantly, vinegar was offered to Christ on the cross, mingled with gall, reflecting the bitterness of His suffering and fulfilling prophetic imagery (Matthew 27:34; Psalms 69:21). Additionally, Proverbs uses vinegar metaphorically to illustrate discomfort and sorrow, comparing it to the irritation caused to teeth and eyes or to a harsh burden on the heart (Proverbs 10:26; 25:20).
